scope: Focused r1 hero/catalogue viewport originals only; exact 20-file list below

findings.observation: At 320/390/768/1440 the title, close control, visible choices, count/reset and Apply remain readable with consistent panel grid. No title/action crossing or missing title fragment was observed.

Catalogue modal matches the home filter system. Reviewed first-row property cards align; visible title phrases and price baselines remain readable. Grid-focused content captures intentionally scroll the preceding count/sort row underneath the fixed site header.

findings.resolution: Parent live-browser native Range probe disproved text clipping. Shrink-to-fit is correct; no hero CSS change was requested.
findings.proofSource: Parent /root live-browser DOM Range measurement reported in the current collaboration thread; no separate Range receipt path was supplied.

findings.resolution: Root diagnostic measured first Close → Shift+Tab → BODY with document.hasFocus=false, then Tab → first Close with document.hasFocus=true. Background controls did not receive focus. The authorized harness adjustment permits only that browser-chrome boundary and requires immediate Tab return inside an open modal; per-key focus receipts were added.

Root diagnostic identified a CSSTransition on dialog scrollbar-color, duration/endTime 0.01ms, identical keyframes; panel opacity1 and transform none. Runtime reduced-motion rule disables dialog transitions explicitly. The strict zero-finite-animation assertion remains unchanged.

limitations: The r1 focused functional run failed early in modal checks. This receipt does not convert those failures into a machine pass.
The four reduced hero PNGs were incomplete-state captures; their original loaded/accepted flags are preserved and they are identified individually.
Lower filter sections, invalid-price/error states, catalogue Apply/empty/linked-invalid states and final r2 modal framing have not yet been reviewed here.
No final all-canonical-page overview or WebKit focused acceptance is implied.
Screenshots bind the r1 source commit. Later fixes and the final source require their own current run evidence.
This is viewport-level visual review, not a claim of inspecting every pixel of every full page or judging animation smoothness from still images.
